title: The Perfect System
objectives: Master the use and formation of the perfect and pluperfect tenses
Understand and apply the concept of reduplication
Read advanced Greek literature with comprehension of perfect system

grammar.explanation: The Greek perfect expresses a present state resulting from a completed action. It is formed with reduplication (repeating initial consonant + ε) and special perfect endings. The pluperfect adds augment and secondary endings.
rules: Vowel-initial verbs: lengthening instead of reduplication
Perfect aspect: completed action with present relevance

exercises.question: Parse 'λέλυκεν'
hints: Reduplication λε- + stem λυ- + perfect ending -κεν

readingPassage.greek: ταῦτα γέγραπται ἵνα πιστεύσητε. οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθής ἐστιν ἡ μαρτυρία αὐτοῦ.
readingPassage.translation: These things have been written so that you may believe. We know that his testimony is true.
notes: οἴδαμεν: perfect with present meaning 'we know'
